name: Ground control program and geotechnical review
summary: Rock in an underground mine can fall from the back or walls, so the mine keeps a ground control program that sets how every opening is supported and checked. The geotechnical engineer reviews stope designs before release, inspects headings with shift supervisors when ground looks poor, audits installed bolts and investigates falls of ground and seismic events. Each review ends with a sign-off, a support instruction to the crews, or a change to the standard. The work is slow and error-prone because one engineer on a two-week rotation carries it, underground inspections need travel and a supervisor at the same time, and urgent events push routine reviews back.

baseline.org_archetype: A 600 tpd underground gold mine in northern Ontario with one site geotechnical engineer, consultant reviews once a year, and 14/14 rotations.
baseline.notes: One case is one geotechnical review of any type: stope design, heading inspection, support audit, fall of ground investigation or standard revision.

trigger: A stope design is submitted, a supervisor reports poor ground, a support audit is due, a fall of ground or seismic event occurs, or a standard needs revising.
end_state: The stope design is signed off, a support instruction is installed and recorded, an investigation is closed, or a revised standard is in force.

volume.seasonality: No marked seasonality; volume rises when mining moves into new, deeper or poorer ground.

evidence.note: Organisation file volume; consistent with 4-9 stope designs a month plus inspections, audits and events.

surge.cause: seismic activity or a run of poor ground in a new mining block

evidence.note: Reference mine had a stope geotechnical problem in Q4 2020 resolved within the month; comparable mine manages seismicity actively. Frequency and multiplier are the author's estimate.

Hands-on time in this file is about 9.4 hours per review, or about 235 hours a month at 25 reviews, which is 1.8 FTE at 130 productive hours. The organisation file has a headcount of one; see assumptions.
Joint heading inspections, line-up instructions and barricading after a fall of ground.
Revises stope designs returned by the geotechnical review; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Reviews investigation reports and approves changes to the ground control standard; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Briefs crews on revised support standards; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Incident, inspection and training records system

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Receive and sort the review request
steps.description: The geotechnical engineer picks up the request from the stope release queue, a supervisor's call or shift report about bad ground, the weekly ground support records or an incident report. He decides what kind of review it is and how urgent, and logs it in his review tracker.

error.defect_description: Urgency misjudged, so a deteriorating heading waits behind routine work.

next.condition: heading ground conditions or support change request
fall of ground or seismic event

evidence.note: Mix of review types is the author's estimate for 25 reviews a month at a 600 tpd mine with 4-9 stope designs a month (organisation file). The long tail of the wait is the engineer being off rotation, when the chief engineer or a phone call with photos covers urgent items.

steps.name: Review stope design against rock mass data
steps.description: The engineer opens the stope design in the planning software and checks the stope dimensions, hangingwall and footwall exposure, brow and pillar sizes against the rock mass quality mapped in nearby development. He compares the design with the agreed mining sequence and with how neighbouring stopes behaved.

error.defect_description: A weak structure crossing the hangingwall is missed.

evidence.note: Open stoping with sequence chosen for stress management at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Run stability and support analysis
steps.description: The engineer runs a stability-graph or wedge analysis for the stope walls and back and designs cable bolting for brows and hangingwalls where needed, aiming for the factor of safety the ground control program sets. He checks the expected overbreak against the dilution allowance used in the reserve.

error.defect_description: Joint orientation input wrong, understating wedge size.

evidence.note: Wedge analysis, Unwedge and factors of safety of 1.2 and 1.5 at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Write the geotechnical assessment
steps.description: The engineer writes the geotechnical assessment: allowed spans, cable bolt pattern, sequence and fill requirements, and any hold points. He either accepts the design as drawn or returns it to the planning engineer with required changes.

error.defect_description: Assessment wording ambiguous on a hold point.

evidence.note: Share of designs returned is the author's estimate; the organisation file notes that rework on stope designs is common.

steps.name: Planning engineer revises the stope design
steps.description: The mine planning engineer changes the stope shape, splits it into smaller stopes or adds a pillar or cable bolting to meet the assessment, then resubmits it. Changes can also move the drill rings and the stope's tonnes and grade.

error.defect_description: Revision introduces a new conflict with development.

evidence.note: Rework loop between engineering and ground control from general practice.

steps.name: Travel underground to the heading
steps.description: The engineer signs in at the lamp room, rides the cage or ramp vehicle to the level and drives a utility vehicle to the heading, arranging to meet the shift supervisor there by radio. Travel to deeper levels can take most of an hour each way.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Underground travel times for a 600-1,000 m deep mine; the wait is for a vehicle and a supervisor free in the same shift.

steps.name: Inspect the heading with the shift supervisor
steps.description: The supervisor and engineer examine the back and walls from under supported ground, sound and scale loose rock, look for cracking, bagging mesh, plate loading and water, and check the bolt pattern against the standard. The supervisor points out what the crew reported.

error.defect_description: Loose not sounded behind mesh is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 (Mines and Mining Plants): examination of ground conditions and no work under unsupported ground; company ground control program

evidence.note: Support classes, bolt pattern and one hole one bolt policy at a comparable mine; legal basis from general knowledge because the Ontario e-Laws text could not be opened.

steps.name: Map structure and rate the rock mass
steps.description: The engineer maps joint sets, faults and shear zones in the heading, estimates a rock mass rating, takes photos and marks positions on a level plan. He notes how the structures line up with the heading direction and planned stopes.
outputs: structural map and rock mass rating

error.defect_description: Rock mass rating is optimistic for the support class chosen.

evidence.note: Standard face mapping practice for ground control engineers.

steps.name: Decide the support class
steps.description: Back on surface the engineer compares the rating and observations with the support classes in the ground control standard and decides whether standard support is enough or the heading needs heavier support such as cable bolts, straps, shotcrete or a shorter round.
inputs: structural map and rock mass rating

error.defect_description: Standard support kept where enhanced support was needed.

evidence.note: Five support classes with escalation for rockburst-prone ground at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Issue the ground support instruction
steps.description: The engineer writes a short support instruction with the area, the support class, the bolt type and pattern, and any cable bolting or rehabilitation, with a sketch, and sends it to the mine captain and the shift supervisors. He posts it at the line-up room so every crew sees it.

error.defect_description: Instruction names the wrong cross-cut or chainage.

evidence.note: Written instructions under the ground control program are common practice.

steps.name: Brief crews and confirm the support is installed
steps.description: At the next line-up the shift supervisor explains the instruction to the bolter and development crews and assigns the work. After installation he checks the heading and records the support installed on the shift report before the heading is released for the next round.

error.defect_description: Instruction not passed to the opposite crew at shift change.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 (Mines and Mining Plants): examination of ground conditions and no work under unsupported ground; company ground control program

evidence.note: Line-ups happen at the start of each 12-hour shift, so the wait is up to one shift.

steps.name: Pull ground support records and test results
steps.description: The engineer collects the bolter shift records, bolt counts by heading, pull-test results and shotcrete thickness checks for the period from the shift sheets and compares them with the support required in each heading. He chooses headings to check in person.

error.defect_description: Records with missing bolt counts are not followed up.

evidence.note: Quality control of installed ground support is part of an Ontario ground control program (from general knowledge; the regulation text could not be opened).

steps.name: Pull-test bolts and check support underground
steps.description: The engineer and a helper travel to the sampled headings, pull-test a set of bolts with a hydraulic jack, measure shotcrete thickness and check plates, mesh overlap and spacing. Results go into a field book.

error.defect_description: Test bolts chosen only in easy-to-reach places.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 (Mines and Mining Plants): examination of ground conditions and no work under unsupported ground; company ground control program

evidence.note: Pull testing practice from general knowledge; the wait is for a utility vehicle and scissor lift.

steps.name: Evaluate compliance with the standard
steps.description: The engineer compares test loads, spacing and coverage with the standard and lists headings that fall short. Nonconforming headings get a corrective support instruction; the rest are recorded as compliant.

error.defect_description: A failed test is averaged away.

evidence.note: Share of audits with findings is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Barricade the area and report the event
steps.description: After a fall of ground or a felt seismic event the shift supervisor withdraws people, barricades and posts the area, and reports it by radio to the mine captain, the safety coordinator and the geotechnical engineer. He fills in the incident report for the safety system.
inputs: fall of ground or seismic event

error.defect_description: Barricade placed too close to the affected area.

control.basis: Ontario Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulation 854: notice of significant falls of ground and preservation of the area

evidence.note: Reporting duties from general knowledge of Ontario mining law; the regulation pages could not be opened.

steps.name: Review seismic data and event details
steps.description: The engineer reviews the event location and magnitude from the seismic monitoring system where it covers the area, the blast records and recent support work, and sets the re-entry conditions and quiet period before anyone inspects the area.

error.defect_description: Re-entry allowed before the post-event activity has settled.

evidence.note: Comparable mine monitors seismicity 24/7 and issues post-blast reports every 12 hours.

steps.name: Inspect the event site underground
steps.description: When re-entry conditions are met the engineer travels to the area with the supervisor, inspects from supported ground, measures the size of the fall, photographs damaged support and judges whether the failure follows a structure. He decides how the area must be made safe.

error.defect_description: Hidden damage to support beyond the fall is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 (Mines and Mining Plants): examination of ground conditions and no work under unsupported ground; company ground control program

evidence.note: The wait is the quiet period and barricade before re-entry.

steps.name: Write the investigation and rehabilitation report
steps.description: The engineer writes up the cause, the size and the support performance, attaches the survey of the cavity, and recommends rehabilitation, support changes for similar ground and any change to the mining sequence. The report goes to the safety coordinator for the incident file.

error.defect_description: Root cause stated as poor installation without testing other causes.

evidence.note: Investigation practice from general knowledge.

steps.name: Record the review and close it
steps.description: The engineer records the outcome in the ground control files: the heading, rating, support class, instruction and photos, and updates the level plan of ground conditions. He closes the request in his tracker.
inputs: support decision or QC findings or confirmed installation

error.defect_description: Record not updated, so the next review lacks history.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854: records of ground conditions and support under the ground control program

evidence.note: Record-keeping duty from general knowledge; regulation text not opened.

steps.name: Sign off the stope design
steps.description: The engineer signs the stope release form for ground control, attaching the geotechnical assessment and noting any hold points such as cable bolting before blasting. The signed package goes back to the planning engineer for operations and geology signatures.
outputs: signed geotechnical section of stope release

error.defect_description: Hold point not carried onto the release form.

control.basis: Company stope design and release procedure: geotechnical sign-off before release

evidence.note: Multi-discipline stope release sign-off, as in the organisation file's stope design process.

steps.name: Draft a revision of the ground control standard
steps.description: Prompted by the annual consultant review, an investigation or new ground at depth, the engineer drafts changes to the ground control standard: support classes, bolt types, patterns, cable bolting rules and quality control checks. He checks the bolts and mesh are stocked before proposing them.

error.defect_description: New pattern not tested against equipment the bolters use.

evidence.note: Annual ground control reviews by qualified consultants and regular stress modelling at a comparable mine.

steps.name: Technical services manager reviews the investigation
steps.description: The technical services manager reads the investigation report, questions the cause and the recommended rehabilitation, and agrees changes to support or sequence with the mine superintendent. He sends it back for more work when the cause is not supported.

error.defect_description: Recommendation accepted without a completion date.

evidence.note: Management review of fall of ground investigations from general practice.

steps.name: Approve the revised standard
steps.description: The technical services manager reviews the draft standard with the mine superintendent and the joint health and safety committee representative and signs it into the ground control program. About one draft in five goes back for changes.

error.defect_description: Superseded standard left in the line-up room.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854: written ground control program kept current for the mine

evidence.note: Approval route is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Brief crews on the revised standard
steps.description: The mine trainer adds the change to the task training material and briefs each crew at line-ups over a full rotation cycle, collecting sign-off sheets. Old copies are removed from the line-up rooms.

error.defect_description: One crew on the opposite rotation is missed.

evidence.note: Briefing both rotations takes two to four weeks on a 14/14 schedule.

exceptions.name: Stope design returned for changes
exceptions.description: The review finds spans or brows that need a smaller stope, a pillar or cable bolting, and the planning engineer revises the design.

exceptions.name: Audit finds nonconforming support
exceptions.description: Pull tests or spacing checks fail and a corrective instruction is issued to the crews.

exceptions.name: Fall of ground investigation
exceptions.description: The area is barricaded, re-entry waits for a quiet period, and the investigation leads to rehabilitation and support changes.

exceptions.name: Engineer off rotation
exceptions.description: Requests arriving while the only geotechnical engineer is off site wait, are handled by phone, or are covered by the chief engineer.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from request to closed review
benchmarks.population: Mixed geotechnical reviews at a single underground mine

evidence.note: Author's estimate: stope reviews must keep pace with weekly stope release and heading reviews close within a shift or two; investigations take two weeks or more.

pain_points.description: One geotechnical engineer on a 14/14 rotation means half the month has no one on site; requests wait or are judged by phone from photos.

evidence.note: Organisation file headcount of one with field_rotation shift pattern.

pain_points.description: Underground inspections need a vehicle and a supervisor free at the same time, and travel takes a large share of the inspection.

evidence.note: General knowledge of underground travel and supervisor workload.

pain_points.description: Support instructions pass by line-up and paper, so a crew on the other shift or rotation can miss them.

evidence.note: Paper line-up boards in the organisation file systems list.

pain_points.description: Stope design rework between engineering and ground control delays stope release and can cost grade when stopes fail.

evidence.note: A stope geotechnical problem hurt grade at the reference mine in Q4 2020.

sources.title: Macassa Mine NI 43-101 Technical Report (April 2019), exhibit 99.20
sources.publisher: Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Comparable Ontario underground gold mine, section 15.5: back support checked with two-dimensional wedge analysis and Unwedge for 3D; minimum factor of safety 1.2 for short-term and 1.5 for long-term headings; five support classes with bolts on a 1.2 m by 1.2 m dice-five pattern; one hole one bolt policy; support to within 1 m of the sill unless ground control approves 1.5 m; 24/7 seismic monitoring by ground control and security with post-blast seismicity reports every 12 hours and bi-weekly mXrap hazard reports; annual ground control reviews by qualified consultants; regular numerical stress modelling; class D support for rockburst-prone headings

sources.title: Island Gold Mine NI 43-101 Technical Report (Phase III expansion), exhibit 99.1
sources.publisher: Alamos Gold Inc. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Comparable Wawa-area underground mine: longitudinal and transverse open stoping, move to a centre-out stoping sequence to support improved mining stress management, paste fill justified partly by geotechnical de-risking, stope dilution of 15-50 percent by sector and method

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Production Results; Provides 2021 Guidance
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (news release, via Yahoo Finance)
sources.supports: Reference mine Q4 2020: geotechnical problems in one underground stope hurt grade performance and were resolved within the month

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (salary times 1.30 for staff roles, 1.35 for hourly roles).

The geotechnical engineer's hands-on time in this file averages about 9.4 hours per review, or about 235 hours a month at 25 reviews (1.8 FTE). One person on a 14/14 rotation is on site about 168 hours a month and away the other half, so the file states 1.8 FTE: in practice a second geotechnical engineer or ground control technologist works the opposite rotation, or the chief engineer and a consultant absorb the overflow. The organisation file's headcount of one is reported as too low.

Ontario Regulation 854 duties (workplace examination of ground, ground control program, records, reporting of falls of ground) are described from general knowledge because the e-Laws and ministry pages returned errors; those controls carry tier C evidence.
The seismic monitoring step assumes a microseismic system covers the main mining area, as at the comparable mine; whether the reference mine had one in 2019-2022 was not confirmed.
Mine engineer, technical services manager and trainer take part but are not listed for this process in the organisation file.
